brief: Goldman's TMT specialist recaps the firm's Communacopia conference. Micro datapoints were upbeat: Visa and Mastercard said August was consistent with July, LYV and TKO reported live event demand intact, enterprise demand was steady on AI-era tech stack modernization, and semiconductor supply and demand showed no sign of cooling. The note frames investor stance as tension. Bottom-up datapoints are constructive, with tight supply and demand, robust token demand and faster product innovation, so negatives are hard to find, but top-down debates persist out of summer volatility, rates and geopolitical uncertainty, midterm policy risk and the law of large numbers. Security was the largest conference theme, with NVDA's Jensen Huang calling cybersecurity the next major AI use case, PANW describing a multi-model fabric and DELL citing cyber risk as a hardware upgrade catalyst. Data infra software (NET, SNOW, DT, DDOG, MDB) is favored because it is less tied to capex yet still benefits from inference adoption, which makes peak-spend debates less restrictive. Networking demand, an analog semi recovery and the NDX's 4+ month consolidation are left as open questions. This reports conference commentary rather than arguing a house forecast.
